message.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Electro-optical photonic integrated circuits (PICs) based on lithium niobate (LiNbO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    ) have demonstrated the vast capabilities of materials with a high Pockels coefficient
                    <jats:sup>1,2</jats:sup>
                    . They enable linear and high-speed modulators operating at complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor voltage levels
                    <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>
                    to be used in applications including data-centre communications
                    <jats:sup>4</jats:sup>
                    , high-performance computing and photonic accelerators for AI
                    <jats:sup>5</jats:sup>
                    . However, industrial use of this technology is hindered by the high cost per wafer and the limited wafer size. The high cost results from the lack of existing high-volume applications in other domains of the sort that accelerated the adoption of silicon-on-insulator (SOI) photonics, which was driven by vast investment in microelectronics. Here we report low-loss PICs made of lithium tantalate (LiTaO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    ), a material that has already been adopted commercially for 5G radiofrequency filters
                    <jats:sup>6</jats:sup>
                    and therefore enables scalable manufacturing at low cost, and it has equal, and in some cases superior, properties to LiNbO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    . We show that LiTaO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    can be etched to create low-loss (5.6 dB m
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ) PICs using a deep ultraviolet (DUV) stepper-based manufacturing process
                    <jats:sup>7</jats:sup>
                    . We demonstrate a LiTaO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    Mach–Zehnder modulator (MZM) with a half-wave voltage–length product of 1.9 V cm and an electro-optic bandwidth of up to 40 GHz. In comparison with LiNbO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    , LiTaO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    exhibits a much lower birefringence, enabling high-density circuits and broadband operation over all telecommunication bands. Moreover, the platform supports the generation of soliton microcombs. Our work paves the way for the scalable manufacture of low-cost and large-volume next-generation electro-optical PICs.
                  </jats:p>
